scope: B2 php-control-flow publication candidate compared with the completed PHP Arrays pilot; LAB evidence only.

interactionMetadata.note: PHP Arrays predates the interaction-opportunity contract, so absence is not measured zero. B2 records four metadata-only opportunities and implements no UI.

recurringProblems: Passing code does not guarantee that explanatory prose is scoped precisely enough.
Both first reviews found an overbroad sentence around a correct example: result type in PHP Arrays and the int/float zero boundary in PHP control flow.
Type, input-shape and return-contract boundaries need explicit wording even in beginner material.
A small hash-bound prose correction followed by a new full Critic pass avoided unnecessary Writer regeneration and PHP reruns.

conclusions: Treat Humanizer as a constrained editorial pass, never as a source of technical facts or an autonomous rewrite loop.
It must preserve evidence-qualified boundaries such as this example, this input type and these runtimes instead of smoothing them into universal claims.
Measure its value by human readability findings; neither pilot recorded readability time or user-comprehension data.
B2 shows that 2-4 opportunities can be attached to section IDs without coupling editorial production to UI implementation.
Future interactions should bind prompts and expected concepts to the reviewed article hash and must not imply that unexecuted learner variants passed runtime verification.
No implementation decision follows until user value, accessibility and maintenance cost are measured.
Separate unsupported corpus claims from genuine technical unknowns; popularity and cross-language analogies were removable noise, not research gaps.
Record excluded contexts explicitly: object comparison, foreach references, nested break/continue, return at file scope and security-sensitive input handling.
Promote a gap to shared knowledge only after repeated evidence across articles; two pilots are enough to observe a pattern, not to define an autonomous Knowledge Gap module.

limitations: Elapsed time, model-token usage, monetary cost, human reading time and learning outcomes were not measured and remain null.
Document, fact and assertion counts describe scope, not semantic difficulty or quality by themselves.
The pilots used different source counts and topic breadth, so the comparison is descriptive, not a benchmark.
